rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the heaters of oxygen tank No. 2 ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)" The tank's thermostatic switches were built for 28 volts DC, which is the switch-failure link in the chain. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The board's report called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: Which Apollo 11 crew member earned a doctorate on the kind of rendezvous Apollo relied on, and in which year?
rows.answer:
Buzz Aldrin, the Apollo 11 lunar module pilot, earned his doctorate in 1963. His MIT thesis was on manned orbital rendezvous [[buzz-aldrin]] "[stated] Earned an MIT doctorate in 1963 with a thesis on manned orbital rendezvous (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

Apollo's mission mode was lunar orbit rendezvous, chosen in 1962, and it required a separate lander [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] Required a separate lander, which became the lunar module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The notes link Aldrin to lunar orbit rendezvous as a topic he studied, but they don't say his thesis was on lunar orbit rendezvous specifically, only on manned orbital rendezvous.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter. The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square, while the lunar module's were round, so an adapter was needed to fit one to the other [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

Engineers devised it from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The crew built it from radioed instructions [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The notes do not give the detailed step-by-step assembly or the dimensions of the parts.
